headline: Kiwi Return to Wellington Hills After 150 Years
meta_description: More than 250 kiwi have returned to New Zealand hills after 150 years, thanks to iwi and community effort across 24,000 hectares.
summary_short: A conservation triumph: over 250 kiwi birds have returned to the Wellington region after an absence of 150 years through an iwi and community-led restoration effort.
body:
More than 250 kiwi birds have returned to the hills around Wellington, New Zealand, marking a remarkable recovery after 150 years of absence from the region.

The achievement spans 24,000 hectares and represents a collaborative effort led by iwi—indigenous Māori communities—working alongside local residents. The scale of the project underscores how large-scale, community-driven conservation can reverse historical losses. With over 300 kiwi now living in the Wellington area, the birds are establishing populations in terrain they had vanished from generations ago.

For conservationists and New Zealanders, the milestone signals hope for native species recovery. Kiwi, flightless birds found nowhere else in the world, face ongoing threats from predators and habitat loss. This regional success demonstrates that protection and restoration efforts can succeed when communities unite behind a shared goal.
quick_facts: More than 250 kiwi returned after 150-year absence
Over 300 kiwi now live in Wellington region
Iwi and community effort spans 24,000 hectares
Project centered around Wellington, New Zealand hills
